summary: Wilkes-Barre depositor who pursued the failed banker F. V. Rockafellow through the courts and died in 1897; her kinship to John is unproven.
bio:
Anna Meier, also recorded as Annie or Maria Meier, lived in Wilkes-Barre, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania. She was a depositor at the bank of F. V. Rockafellow on its last day and lost $700 when it failed. She then pursued the embezzlement case against Rockafellow from 1893 to 1897, carrying it to the Superior Court, which in 1897 reversed a lower-court ruling; she told the judge in open court that she "did not think justice had been done". She died in July 1897 after a fall on her way home from visiting friends on Grove Street.

She was not John's ancestor Maria A. Meier, and whether she was related to the family at all is unproven.
